newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada bonds end sharply lower but outperform U.S..
newsitem.headline: Canada bonds end sharply lower but outperform U.S..

text.p: Canadian bonds ended a shortened session sharply lower on Friday, pulled down with U.S. Treasuries on stronger-than-expected U.S. economic and employment data.

"When the ten o'clock numbers came out the bottom fell out. I think those instilled the fear in a lot of people's minds that this market is overcooked," said Jeoff Hall, Canadian market analyst with Technical Data. "Canada just kept following the U.S."
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond plunged C$1.59 to C$121.09 to yield 6.405 percent.

The U.S. 30-year bond fell 1-26/32 to yield 6.44 percent. The negative spread between the bonds widened to four basis points from one basis point at Tuesday's close. Analysts said the Canadian market did not sell off as badly because there were less investors with long positions.
"I don't think Canada was as overbought as the U.S. was," said Hall. "Exposure was more limited."

North American fixed-income markets initially weakened on Friday after the U.S. Labor Department reported that the economy there added 316,000 new jobs in July and the jobless rate stood at 4.8 percent.
Economists had forecast non-farm payrolls growth of 193,000 and a jobless rate of 4.9 percent.
But a report showing that the U.S. National Association of Purchasing Management's July index soared to 58.6 in July from 55.7 in June triggered a major selloff.

"It seems to have taken the purchasing managers' index, with its pretty strong numbers, to give it the real downward boost, and away it went," said Dawn Desjardins, a fixed-income analyst with J.P. Morgan Canada.
In other prices, Canada's 10-year benchmark bond fell C$0.99 to C$109.92 to yield 5.902 percent. The U.S. 10-year bond fell 1-6/32 to yield 6.17 percent.
The negative spread between the bonds widened to 27 basis points from 23 basis points at Thursday's close.
